newsitem.title: USA: California cabbies say no-sweat rules stink.
newsitem.headline: California cabbies say no-sweat rules stink.

text.p: Taxi drivers love tips, but some cabbies are getting unwanted advice from passengers too -- like "take a shower!" or "brush your teeth."
In this desert town where summer temperatures can soar to a sticky 120 degrees F (49 Celcius), the atmosphere inside a cab can be critical.
So the Palm Springs Regional Airport Commission stepped in on Wednesday, following complaints about less-than-savory personal hygiene of some drivers serving the airport.
The Airport Commission was considering a hygienic code for the sweaty drivers -- including washing with soap, brushing teeth with toothpaste and using breath mints daily.
But with only a "vocal minority" of drivers present at the Commission meeting on Wednesday, introduction of the rules was put off.
"The Commission decided to do nothing until we can meet with all the drivers," Allen Smoot, the airport manager said.
"These regulations are crazy. I was surprised they didn't tell me what brand of toothpaste to use," cabbie George Turner told the Los Angeles Times.
And Rafael Meghnagi wondered: "What kind of man chews itsy-bitsy breath mints?"
